title: Sell Mineral Rights in Catherine, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Catherine, CO
metaDescription: Catherine sits in rural Garfield County Piceance gas territory. See how tight-sands geology and small legacy leases affect what your mineral interest is worth.
heroLead: Catherine is a small, rural area of Garfield County within the broader Piceance Basin footprint, where mineral ownership tends to trace back to the same ranch and homestead-era deeds common across this part of the Western Slope.
intro: Gas development in this part of the county has followed the boom-and-slowdown pattern typical of the Piceance Basin generally — significant activity in the mid-2000s tied to strong natural gas prices, followed by a much quieter pace since. Whether a specific tract near Catherine has an active lease or production history depends on its exact position relative to where operators concentrated that earlier development.

sections.heading: Tight-gas economics in a quieter cycle
paragraphs: Williams Fork tight-sands wells in this area were developed heavily when gas prices supported the completion costs; since then, activity has been far more selective. That doesn't mean an existing well has stopped paying — tight-gas wells often maintain a long, low-volume production tail for years — but it does mean new development on undrilled acreage is less certain than it was fifteen years ago.

sections.heading: What determines value on a Catherine-area tract
paragraphs: For a producing interest, we build from actual royalty statements and current gas pricing realizations. For a non-producing tract, we weigh the area's historical activity level and any current permit filings, pricing conservatively given the slower recent pace without assuming the tract has no future potential at all.

sections.heading: Comparing checks across the Piceance versus DJ Basin
paragraphs: If you've compared notes with relatives or acquaintances who hold Weld County oil minerals, don't expect the numbers to line up. Gas royalty economics run on different volume and pricing mechanics than an oil well's, and the Piceance Basin's more recent slowdown compared to the DJ Basin's continued Wattenberg activity means development odds for undrilled acreage also differ meaningfully between the two areas.

faqs.question: My family's gas royalties have dropped a lot over the years — is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, tight-gas wells decline steeply after an initial peak before settling into a long, lower-volume tail, and gas pricing also swings with the market. We factor both into any offer.

faqs.question: Is new development likely on undrilled Catherine-area acreage?
faqs.answer: Less certain than during the mid-2000s boom, though not ruled out. We check current permitting activity against your specific legal description.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests with old, inactive leases?
faqs.answer: Yes, we review lease status and current production data directly rather than relying on the age of the original lease alone.

faqs.question: Why does my Piceance gas interest seem to be valued differently than a friend's Weld County oil minerals?
faqs.answer: Gas and oil royalty economics work differently, and the two basins are currently at different points in their development cycles, which both affect value independently of your specific ownership.
